$comment: The room's MCP tools, written once. Placeholders: {{signals}} (signals.json), {{rotate_k}} (policy room.params). callers: "any" seat, "spawners" (roles the workflow lets create seats) or "room" (roles the workflow puts at home in the room); a call from another role is refused, and a seat is listed only the tools its role may call.

seatwork_mail.description: Mail seats of your room, or set a timed wake-up. A mail is delivered between the recipient's turns; a STOP, to a seat below you, ends its running turn and every turn under it at once, and each reads your text next. `wake` has the room mail a WAKE at a set time, which starts a turn though nobody writes.

to.description: `owner`, a seat you launched (its id, the start of its id, or its title), several of them, or `team`: every open seat under you, which reads it with its next mail. A seat with no seat under it may leave it out: its owner. Omit with reply_to. wake: the one seat to wake, yourself when left out.

cc.description: Seats that get a copy to read; it starts no turn of theirs.

reply_to.description: The id of the mail you answer; the answer goes to its sender and joins its thread.

subject.description: Short; opens with one of the room's signals: {{signals}}.

body.description: Self-contained: the recipient may read it hours later.

needs.description: What you need back; `decision` says you are stopped until it comes.

thread.description: The work-store issue this mail is about.

key.description: Your own name for this mail: sent again with the same key and text, it stays one mail.

action.description: `send` is the default and needs `subject` and `body`; `wakes` lists the wake-ups for you or set by you; `unwake` cancels one.

at.description: wake: an ISO time with its zone.

in_minutes.description: wake: minutes from now, instead of `at`.

note.description: wake: what you do when it comes; the body of the WAKE.

seatwork_inbox.description: Read your mailbox. With nothing given: the mail held for you, what arrived while you were busy and what starts no turn of its own, marked read. `id`, `thread` and search also reach the mail of the seats under you.

view.description: new is the default. all: what you received. sent: what you sent and how each delivery stands. owed: asks waiting for your answer, and yours waiting for one. search: with `q`.

id.description: One mail, with its whole body.

thread.description: An issue id, or the thread a mail names: its mails, a line each.

q.description: search: the words to look for.

signal.description: all, search: only mail whose subject opens with this signal.

since.description: all, sent, search: only mail after this ISO time.

bodies.description: thread: the mails whole, not a line each.

project.description: search, thread: another project's mail, by its folder or name, or all; for a seat that reads every project.

seatwork_projects.description: The project registry: every project Paseo knows, registered or not, with its root, whether its mission and law exist, and its model table.

seatwork_register_project.description: Register a project Paseo already has, with its mission, law and model table. Call again with `mission`, `law` or `models` to replace them.

path.description: The project's root, or its name in Paseo (see seatwork_projects).

name.description: Registry name, letters digits dashes. Default: the Paseo name.

mission.description: What the project is for and what done looks like, a few lines of markdown.

models.description: Only the differences from ROOM_DIR/models.json, same shape: objects merge, lists and values replace, null removes a key; {} takes the project's own table out.

seatwork_unregister_project.description: Take a project out of the registry: no seat of the room starts in it after that. Its `.seatwork/` files stay, and seatwork_register_project brings it back.

project.description: The project's registry name, or its root.

seatwork_room.description: Run the room itself; `do` is the action. health: the last day's incidents by district, open traces, and the readings there are. A reading's name: that district's numbers now. log: the room's log, newest first. incidents: troubles of the last `days`, each with its id, how often, how often in the last hour, and where it stands. ack, snooze, resolve: set where incident `id` stands. trace: open one on an `incident`, or add a note to trace `id`; traces: the open ones; close: end one. policy: the keys you may tune, their values and ranges, the last changes. tune: set one key. revert: undo change `id`. skill: add, remove or list a role's skills; its seats get a change at their next start.

days.description: incidents: the window, a few days at most.

id.description: ack, snooze, resolve: the incident; trace, close: the trace; revert: the change.

note.description: ack, snooze, resolve: why; for resolve, the cause.

hypothesis.description: trace: what you think the cause is.

path.description: tune: the key, as policy lists it.

trace.description: tune: the trace the change serves.

role.description: skill: the role whose seats get it.

name.description: skill: its name, lowercase words joined by dashes.

files.description: skill add: each file's path in the skill's folder, .md or .txt, to its text; one is SKILL.md.

source.description: skill add: where it came from: `license` own for yours, with `repo` and `commit` when taken from elsewhere.

revisit.description: tune: a key reverted twice lately, tuned again on new evidence.

evidence.description: tune, revert: what you read and measured.

seatwork_work.description: The project's work store: issues, what each waits for, who holds it. create: one issue, or a whole plan in `issues`. ready: open issues nothing holds back (no open blocker, blocked parent or open child), highest priority first. claim: take an issue to work on. note: a dated line of progress. depend: `id` waits for `on`. show: an issue with its newest comments; comments: the older ones.

id.description: An issue id, or enough of it after the prefix to name one issue.

issues.description: create: several issues in one write, all or none. Each has title and may have key, description, design, acceptance_criteria, write_scope, priority, issue_type, labels, parent, deps; parent and deps may name another's key.

description.description: What is to be done and why, enough for a seat that sees nothing else.

acceptance_criteria.description: The checks that show it is done, a line each.

write_scope.description: The files or folders this issue may change.

parent.description: create: the issue this one is a child of. ready: only what is under this issue.

deps.description: create: what this issue waits for: ids or keys, or {id, type}.

on.description: depend, undepend: the issue `id` waits for.

type.description: depend: blocks by default; discovered-from is for work found on the way.

status.description: list: filter. update: open, in_progress or deferred; closing is `close`.

assignee.description: list: a seat id, or `me`. update: a seat id, `me`, or null to free the issue.

defer_until.description: update: an ISO time before which the issue is not ready.

text.description: note, comment: the line to add.

reason.description: close: what was done, and the commit or the evidence.

if_revision.description: update: the revision you read; the write is refused when the issue has moved on.

unassigned.description: ready: only issues no seat holds.

force.description: close: close over open blockers or children.

skip.description: comments: how many of the newest comments to pass over.

seatwork_graph.description: The project's open issues as a graph; `view` names the reading. triage: what to do first, scored with reasons, and the blockers worth clearing first. next: the one issue to take now; only a claim reserves it. plan: groups no dependency joins, which can run side by side, each with its ready issues and the pairs whose write scopes collide. blockers: from `id` down to what must close first. alerts: an issue held and untouched for long, one holding many back.

id.description: blockers: the issue to start from.

limit.description: triage: how many recommendations (10 by default).

seatwork_safety.description: The room's checks on the work: the hand-in check and the council. ack: keep on purpose one finding of the hand-in check that sent your candidate back; your Owner reads why. council: how each member of the council has read turns lately. label: say whether a `[council]` finding about a seat under you was right. rule: the room's own seat rules on an APPEAL mail. control: for a writer `seat`, a copy of its project at the commit it started on with only its candidate's tests laid in; a new test that passes there does not test the change. copy: for a writer `seat`, the commit it handed in, to run the acceptance evidence apart from the shared tree.

id.description: ack: the finding's id from the returned candidate. label: the council finding's number, after the member's name. rule: the appeal's number.

reason.description: ack: why the finding stays. label: why the finding was right or wrong. rule: why the candidate goes back or stays.

send_back.description: rule: true returns the candidate to its seat.

value.description: label: whether the finding was right.

days.description: council: how many days back; 30 when not given.

seatwork_seats.description: The open seats under you, one line each: role, title and id; its state and for how long; context held and cost; the signal its last turn ended with; the rejections of its task since its last ACCEPT; mail held for it and the answers it owes. A seat past {{rotate_k}}K tokens of context is marked for seatwork_rotate.

seatwork_rotate.description: Replace a seat under you whose context has grown large, as seatwork_seats marks it, with a fresh seat on the same model that continues its work from a handoff the old seat writes.

why.description: One clause the seat is told, such as its context size or the task ahead.

seatwork_adopt.description: Take over a seat handed to you, of a role you may create, whose owner is archived or in your own chain: it then reports to you.

agent_id.description: Id of the seat to adopt (from the handoff).

seatwork_knowledge.description: The room's record of what seats saw, did and said, and the decisions in force; `do` is the action. search: the record, best first. view, expand: entries by `address`. pack: a task's evidence. decide: record a rule a person decided that later work follows. `scope` room or project, by the room's own seat: in force when your turn ends, on the person's words in it, or at once `from` their address. `scope` task, by a seat that briefs: in force at once. To change one, decide again with `replaces_version`. withdraw: end one. list: the decisions in force for you.

q.description: search: the words to look for.

also.description: search: up to four other wordings, which find more.

task.description: search, pack: one task. decide with scope task: the task it binds.

since.description: search: an ISO date, or a time with its zone.

limit.description: search: how many hits (10 by default, 50 at most).

around.description: expand: entries on each side of the address (5 by default, 20 at most).

budget.description: pack: characters of evidence (6000 by default, 20000 at most).

project.description: Another project by folder or name, or room; decide: the bound project.

topic.description: decide, withdraw: a few words; one decision per topic.

statement.description: decide: the whole decision, one sentence.

from.description: decide, withdraw: the address of the person's words.

replaces_version.description: decide, withdraw: the version in force.

new_topic.description: decide: not one of the near topics.

valid_from.description: decide: an ISO date or time with its zone, not ahead of now.

valid_until.description: decide: an ISO date or time with its zone; a task's decision ends after 30 days without one. The replaced one returns.

all.description: list: every room and project decision, for the room's own seat.
